item.title: Security and stability for two families
item.description: TWO families in Ba can now look forward to greater security and stability after receiving new homes through the Government’s Rural Housing Assistance Program. Minister for Rural and Maritime Development Mosese Bulitavu recently commissioned two rural housing projects in Ba, for Ganga Prasad and fellow recipient Jone Lotawa.
item.content:encoded:
TWO families in Ba can now look forward to greater security and stability after receiving new homes through the Government’s Rural Housing Assistance Program.

Minister for Rural and Maritime Development Mosese Bulitavu recently commissioned two rural housing projects in Ba, for Ganga Prasad and fellow recipient Jone Lotawa.

For Mr Prasad, the new home means having a place of his own and greater security for his family, as he had been living with his brother at Wailailai Settlement, outside Ba Town.

“All my life I have never owned a house,” he said.

“For more than 20 years I lived in my brother’s house, and I never thought that one day I would have a home of my own.

“Through the assistance from the Government under the Rural Housing Assistance Program, that dream has finally come true.”

Mr Lotawa said while renting had provided his family with a place to live, owning a home had given them a greater sense of stability and independence.

“Nothing compares to the freedom of owning your own home,” he said.

“For more than a decade, my family and I were renting, and we had to deal with the uncertainties that came with being tenants.”

“Today, that has changed. We finally have a house that belongs to our family.”

Minister Mosese Bulitavu said the two housing projects demonstrated Government’s commitment to improving living conditions for vulnerable families in rural communities.

Both recipients received assistance under Scheme 3 of the RHA Program. Under the scheme, applicants contribute one-sixth of the total project cost, while the Government covers the remaining five-sixths.

The RHA Program provides housing assistance to vulnerable rural households to help improve their living conditions through safe, durable, and adequate homes.

item.title: Firm refutes pay claims
item.description: ENERGY Fiji Ltd’s (EFL)chief executive officer Fatiaki Gibson has hit back at allegations from the Construction Energy and Trade Workers Union of Fiji (CETWUF), asserting that public statements regarding wage delays and executive salary increases are misleading and ignore binding agreements. The response follows claims raised by union national secretary John Paul, who highlighted media reports sho
item.content:encoded:
ENERGY Fiji Ltd’s (EFL)chief executive officer Fatiaki Gibson has hit back at allegations from the Construction Energy and Trade Workers Union of Fiji (CETWUF), asserting that public statements regarding wage delays and executive salary increases are misleading and ignore binding agreements.

The response follows claims raised by union national secretary John Paul, who highlighted media reports showing total remuneration for EFL’s chief executive and executive management group increased from $3.309million in 2024 to $3.756m in 2025 while worker wage adjustments remained pending.

“EFL is unable to understand why CETWUF’s recent correspondence and public statements continue to rely on matters relating to the 2024 and 2025 Logs of Claim, particularly when those matters were fully considered during the arbitration proceedings and are inconsistent with the court’s findings,” Mr Gibson said.

The mediated agreement signed by both parties, he said, locked salaries and wages for a two-year period, meaning the company was legally bound by those terms until new negotiations begin for 2026.

Addressing the ongoing dispute, Mr Gibson noted that the union’s actions had damaged its standing among workers, with union membership within EFL dropping to approximately 25 per cent.

“CETWUF’s repeated disregard of established facts and binding court findings have significantly eroded employee confidence in its representation.”

He said such public claims threatened to mislead union members and the wider community regarding the true status of negotiations.

Mr Gibson affirmed that EFL remains willing to engage with the union on legitimate outstanding matters for 2026.

“As a responsible employer, EFL remains committed to conducting its employment and industrial relations practices in accordance with the Employment Relations Act, the applicable Collective Agreement, and the principles of good faith, fairness, transparency, and mutual respect.”

item.title: Report: Data centre build could create 5000 jobs
item.description: A NEW report on the potential growth of data centres in New Zealand says a large-scale construction program could create about 5000 jobs, with a significant proportion in electrical and mechanical trades. The report by Boston Consulting Group (BCG) said New Zealand could capture up to $120 billion in economic activity from new data centres over the next decade if it moved quickly.
item.content:encoded:
A NEW report on the potential growth of data centres in New Zealand says a large-scale construction program could create about 5000 jobs, with a significant proportion in electrical and mechanical trades.

The report by Boston Consulting Group (BCG) said New Zealand could capture up to $120 billion in economic activity from new data centres over the next decade if it moved quickly.

That is up from the group’s earlier forecast of $70 billion in potential economic gains.

The new forecast is based on a larger future data centre build-out of 1 gigawatt (GW).

BCG said a construction program of that scale could drive economic activity across New Zealand’s supply chain, creating about 3500 jobs during the peak construction period.

It said about 60 per cent of those roles would be in electrical and mechanical trades, while civil trades would account for a further 21 per cent.

The report said that once operational, data centres typically sustain about one role for every megawatt of capacity, resulting in about 1000 ongoing jobs.

BCG New Zealand managing director and partner Kelly Newton, said growing global demand for data centres opened up opportunities for New Zealand.

“Between New Zealand’s natural advantages, renewables development, stable political environment, and growing investor interest, it has the opportunity to move quickly to capture its slice of the global data centre pie, worth approximately $120 billion in economic activity,” Newton said.

Earlier this month, Contact Energy announced it was exploring plans with CDC Data Centres for a potential large-scale 250-megawatt data centre at Stratford in Taranaki.

Meanwhile, in Southland, Datagrid is preparing to build a large-scale data centre at Makarewa, north of Invercargill.

Data Centre development is not without controversy however.

Large builds have faced local opposition in the United States and the Greens have recently called for a one-year moratorium on data centre builds in New Zealand. The Greens have concerns about the potential benefits of data centres and what impact they may have on water and electricity supply.

item.content:encoded:
HONG KONG – Alphabet has raised $A5.5billion ($F8.6b) via its inaugural Australian dollar debt issuance, according to a term sheet seen by Reuters, adding to the hectic pace of fundraising by global technology companies.

The US tech giant raised the amount by issuing 3-, 5-, 10- and 20-year bonds, the term sheet showed. The company set the coupon at 6.9 per cent for the longest tenor bond tranche, according to the term sheet.

Alphabet did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.

Bids received from investors for the $A5.5b ($F8.6b) debt offering were worth more than $A18b (F28b), according to the term sheet, underscoring strong appetite for new notes from tech companies.

Global tech companies are increasingly looking to capital markets to fund their massive AI spending, after having typically relied on their large cash reserves to fund investments.

The companies are expected to spend more than $730billion this year primarily on AI, and the outlay is already squeezing cash flows. Alphabet posted its first-ever negative free cash flow in its second-quarter report in late July.

Alphabet has become the first AI hyperscaler to tap into the Australian dollar debt market and the first US large-cap tech company to issue a “Kangaroo” bond since Apple in 2016.

item.title: Cook Strait disrupts livestock trade
item.description: Livestock transporters say ferry cancellations and fewer working vessels are hurting their businesses. Sailings across Cook Strait have been cancelled on Tuesday, due to strong winds and high swells.
item.content:encoded:
Livestock transporters say ferry cancellations and fewer working vessels are hurting their businesses.

Sailings across Cook Strait have been cancelled on Tuesday, due to strong winds and high swells.

Downlands Deer general manager Kris Orange said he relied on ferries up to five times a week to move livestock between the North and South Islands.

“It’s pretty critical we know what’s going on and, with the number of ferries dropping off, it has made it more tricky,” he said.

On Monday, one of his trucks was scheduled to cross Cook Strait with cattle, but the Bluebridge Connemara ferry broke down and the sailing was rescheduled for Tuesday — and then cancelled, due to weather.

This has knock-on effects. After dropping off the stock, he was meant to pick up other animals, which now have to wait longer.

Orange said there was nothing anyone could do about the weather, but there was little flexibility in the system.

Interislander’s working fleet has dropped to a single ferry – Kaiārahi – for the next couple of months.

“We just don’t have the number of ferries to choose from to get loads away, because there’s not as many ferries sailing.

“We have to take what we can get as far as crossing times and, quite often, that doesn’t really match up with what we want to do.”

Unreliable and reduced crossings cost time and money, he said.

Orange explained, if there was a ferry cancellation, paddocks needed to be rented for the animals – or they needed to go back to the farm, if no facilities were available.

“I’d hate to think what it costs in money terms. I mean, there’s drivers’ wages and diesel and things, but it all adds up to a cost and it’s basically dead money for everybody.”

Orange told RNZ he had to hope there were no “blowouts” with current ferries.

“If something catastrophic was to happen to one of those ferries and it was out of action for more than a few days, it would be disastrous for the livestock industry that does rely on shipping stock north and south, both to freezing works and for breeding purposes.”

He said everyone was waiting for newer ferries to join the fleet.

A Kiwirail spokesperson said Interislander was operating a planned one-ship timetable, while Kaitaki underwent scheduled drydock maintenance in Singapore. Kaitaki was due to return to service on September 27.

They said Interislander only cancelled sailings for safety or operational reasons.

The spokesperson said freight was a core part of Interislander’s role.

Bluebridge has been approached for comment.

item.title: Threat of El Niño disruption
item.description: MILK prices across several commodities have risen at the latest Global Dairy Trade auction. The average price rose almost 2.3 per cent overnight to $US3873 ($F6058). It followed prices holding steady at the last auction with just a 0.1 per cent price increase two weeks ago.
item.content:encoded:
MILK prices across several commodities have risen at the latest Global Dairy Trade auction.

The average price rose almost 2.3 per cent overnight to $US3873 ($F6058). It followed prices holding steady at the last auction with just a 0.1 per cent price increase two weeks ago.

In a note, New Zealand Exchange dairy analyst Rosalind Crickett said it was another bullish result for most dairy commodities.

“Sentiment in the market over the last couple of weeks remains centred around the same thing,” she said.

“While global milk production may have been strong in the year-to-date out of most regions, record high temperatures in the Northern Hemisphere, paired with the potentially strongest El Niño weather on record for the Southern Hemisphere in the months to come, could change the supply side dynamic.”

Adding to this, she said it was a key time for buyers to get orders over the line ahead of the festive season.

The important whole-milk powder price rose 3 per cent to $US3591 ($F5616). It was the same for skim milk powder which rose 7.6 per cent, hovering near 12-month highs seen in May this year.

Crickett said this was “in line with expectations” as there were concerns about future milk production.

“While Europe and the US most recent data showed continued growth, reports on the ground are depicting farmers are already starting to dip into winter feed reserves amid drought conditions.”

Butter meanwhile was down 2 per cent, and anhydrous milk fat was down 6 per cent- attributed to ample global supply of milk fats.

Last week Fonterra lifted its 12-month butter volumes forecast by 4.7 per cent, while US butter was production up 8.5 per cent year on year in June and Europe’s rose 5.4 per cent in May.

Crickett said New Zealand milk production figures due out later this week will likely to confirm the year on year growth story, with on-the-ground anecdotes from farmers around the country as pasture conditions remain robust, and with plenty of supplementary feed to go around currently.

item.title: Boost for global event
item.description: INVESTMENT Fiji has been announced as the silver sponsor for the inaugural CIDESCO Fiji Congress 2026, strengthening efforts to promote Fiji’s beauty, wellness and tourism sectors and attract international investment. The congress scheduled for August 29-31 in Nadi will host delegates from around the world, providing opportunities for knowledge exchange, international partnerships and business dev
item.content:encoded:
INVESTMENT Fiji has been announced as the silver sponsor for the inaugural CIDESCO Fiji Congress 2026, strengthening efforts to promote Fiji’s beauty, wellness and tourism sectors and attract international investment.

The congress scheduled for August 29-31 in Nadi will host delegates from around the world, providing opportunities for knowledge exchange, international partnerships and business development while highlighting the country’s growing wellness economy.

Investment Fiji chief executive officer Kamal Chetty said the organisation was proud to support the congress because it aligned with its focus on sectors with potential for sustainable economic growth, investment and international collaboration.

“The beauty and wellness sector is an emerging contributor to Fiji’s economy, offering opportunities to create skilled employment, strengthen local enterprises and attract high-value investment,” Mr Chetty said.

He said the congress would provide a platform to promote Fiji’s beauty, wellness and tourism industries to an international audience while encouraging new partnerships and business opportunities.

“By partnering with this event, we are helping position Fiji as a competitive wellness destination and demonstrating the innovation, talent and investment potential our country has to offer.”

Nama Fiji and Spa Academy Fiji director Debra Sadranu said the organisation was honoured to welcome Investment Fiji as a silver sponsor.

“Their support demonstrates confidence in Fiji’s beauty and wellness industry and the potential it holds as an important contributor to our economy,” Ms Sadranu said.

She said hosting international delegates would help strengthen relationships and create opportunities in wellness, education, innovation and investment.

“The congress will further position Fiji as a wellness hub in the Pacific while showcasing the expertise and opportunities available across the sector.”

The congress is hosted by Nama Fiji and Spa Academy Fiji, and will bring together international leaders, educators, spa professionals and industry experts to promote excellence in beauty therapy, wellness and sustainability.

Investment Fiji, Nama Fiji and Spa Academy Fiji said they were committed to supporting industry development, encouraging investment and strengthening Fiji’s international reputation as a wellness destination.

item.title: Floating breakfast experience
item.description: A FLOATING breakfast experience popularised by resorts in Bali, and the Maldives has been introduced at Tambua Sands Beach Resort on Fiji’s Coral Coast. In a media statement, the adults-only resort said the breakfast experience allowed guests to have breakfast in their private plunge pools.
item.content:encoded:
A FLOATING breakfast experience popularised by resorts in Bali, and the Maldives has been introduced at Tambua Sands Beach Resort on Fiji’s Coral Coast.

In a media statement, the adults-only resort said the breakfast experience allowed guests to have breakfast in their private plunge pools.

“The meal is served on a floating tray and includes tropical fruit, pastries, juice, coffee, and other island-inspired selections,” the resort stated.

“The experience costs $89 per person. Guests can also request additional food and beverages, dietary accommodations, romantic touches, and arrangements for special occasions at an additional cost.”

Resort manager Angela Bob said the experience was designed to give guests a way to enjoy their surroundings while creating a memorable holiday experience.

“Our guests travel from around the world to experience the beauty of Fiji,” Ms Bob said.

“We wanted to create something unique that allows them to slow down, relax and truly enjoy their surroundings.

“The floating breakfast is more than a meal; it is an experience and a memory.”

Tambua Sands Beach Resort is located on Fiji’s Coral Coast and offers private villas, beachfront accommodation, and plunge pools.

The resort caters to adults and is set among tropical gardens overlooking the beach.

The floating breakfast is available to guests celebrating occasions such as honeymoons, anniversaries, and birthdays, as well as those looking to add a special experience to their stay.
